clues: Jonah's ribbon was neither lavender nor peach.
The rose was tied with neither the white nor the peach ribbon.
Jonah ordered either the rose or the peony.
hints: Which ribbon could Jonah have chosen? Look at his row in the ribbons box and read clue 2.
Use the only choice left: clue 2 leaves Jonah one ribbon, and clue 1 settles Bea's. Now look at the rose and clue 3.
Clue 3 leaves the rose only lavender, which was Cyrus's. So Cyrus ordered the rose, and clue 4 leaves Jonah the peony.

solution.key_idea: Clues 1 and 2 give Jonah the white ribbon and Cyrus the lavender; clue 3 then carries the rose to Cyrus.
steps: Clue 2 leaves Jonah only the white ribbon, and clue 1 gives Bea the peach, so Cyrus chose lavender.
By clue 3, the rose was tied with neither white nor peach, so its ribbon was lavender.
Carry the dot: the lavender ribbon was Cyrus's, so Cyrus ordered the rose.
Clue 4 says Jonah ordered the rose or the peony; the rose is Cyrus's, so Jonah ordered the peony.
That leaves Bea the carnation, tied with her peach ribbon, and Jonah's peony wore white.
solution.epilogue: Mabel handed over every corsage before noon: Jonah's peony with white ribbon, Bea's carnation with peach, and Cyrus's rose with lavender. Then she corrected the spelling on all three slips.

tip: When you finish, check every box: one dot in each row and column, and all three boxes telling the same story.
